title: 'Flock Flocked up'

reading.body:
This is a false-positive failure at the front end of a deployment: an automated licence plate reader flagged a plate as stolen when it was not, and the alert was treated as a fact on which officers acted. The error did not stay inside the camera. It propagated into a traffic stop, a drawn-weapon response, a K-9 deployment, an arrest, and charges, all of which followed from a single misread. The camera's output was consumed as a signal rather than as a candidate match requiring confirmation.

The gap is at the handoff between the system and the people who act on it. Nothing in the reporting shows a verification step between the alert and the stop, such as a human comparing the flagged image against the vehicle in front of them. The camera image showed a Chevy Malibu while the plate was on a red Dodge Ram pickup, a mismatch visible to a person looking at both. Catching this would have required that comparison to happen before the stop escalated, not after.

What is not established is how the misread occurred, whether the system had a known error rate, or whether any officer knew the alert was unverified at the time. The department's own investigation found no wrongdoing in the K-9 use, and charges were later dropped, but the reporting does not establish intent, fault, or what the department concluded about the camera itself.

reports.title: Body cam of TPD officers releasing K-9 on man during traffic stop
Man speaks out after police release K-9 on him during traffic stop: 'Traumatized'
TPD investigation finds no wrongdoing in use of K-9 on man during traffic stop
Charges dropped against man Toledo Police released K-9 on during traffic stop, lawyer says

summary:
Toledo Police released body camera video showing officers drawing guns and using a K-9 on a driver during a traffic stop. The stop happened after a FLOCK camera wrongly flagged a stolen plate. The camera image showed a Chevy Malibu, but the plate was actually on a red Dodge Ram pickup. The driver, Brandon Upchurch, got out with his hands up, then walked onto the grass. He was arrested and charged with resisting arrest and obstruction. Officers later learned the plate was not stolen and that the alert was a misread. Upchurch received medical attention at the scene.

Police said they believed the driver might flee and did not know if he or the passenger had weapons. The department's K-9 policy says handlers should weigh the crime's severity, any immediate threat, and whether a suspect is resisting or hiding before deploying a dog. Multiple officers are under investigation, and the body camera footage was released Monday.
